**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on Surah 57, verse 12:**

﴿On the day you see the believing men and the believing women﴾: this is a temporal adverbial (*zarf*) related to what is connected with it. It is either related to "that is", or to "that", or to His saying, exalted is He, ( ﴿so He multiplies it for him﴾ ), or it is in the accusative by an implied "remember" (*udhkur*), to magnify that day. The seeing is visual sight. The address is to everyone who is able to see, or it is to the chief of those addressed, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him. His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿their light runs before them﴾ is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) from the object of "you see". By "light" is meant its literal reality, as is manifest from the suns of the reports, and to this the majority (*al-Jumhur*) went. The meaning is: their light runs when they run.

﴿before them and on their right hands﴾: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: "They will be given their light according to the measure of their deeds. They will pass over the Sirat, and among them is one whose light is like a mountain, and among them is one whose light is like a palm tree, and the least of them in light is one whose light is on his big toe; it is extinguished once and kindled another time." Its apparent meaning is that this light occurs at the passing over the Sirat. Some said: it occurs before that and continues with them when they pass over the Sirat. In the reports there is what requires this, as you will hear shortly, if Allah, exalted is He, wills. The intended meaning is that it will be for them in two directions: the direction in front and the direction of the right. These two were specified because the blessed are given their books of deeds from these two directions, just as the wretched are given them from their left sides and behind their backs. In al-Bahr: the apparent meaning is that the light is of two kinds: a light before them that illuminates the direction they face, and a light on their right hands that illuminates what surrounds them of directions. The majority said: the light is originally on their right hands, and what is before them is the spreading radiance from that. It was also said: the *ba'* (in "bi-aymanihim") is in the sense of *'an* (from), i.e. "from their right hands", and the meaning is in all their directions. The right hands were mentioned because of their nobility. End of quotation. And to this meaning there bears witness

[p. 175]

what Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and Ibn Mardawayh reported from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, that he heard Abu Dharr and Abu al-Darda say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I will be the first to be permitted to prostrate on the Day of Resurrection, and the first to be permitted to raise his head. I will raise my head and look before me, behind me, to my right and to my left, and I will recognize my community among the nations." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will you recognize them among the nations, from Noah, peace be upon him, until your community?" He said: "They are radiant, with white marks from the traces of ablution, and no one other than them will have this. I will recognize them by their books being given to them in their right hands, and I will recognize them by their mark on their faces from the trace of prostration, and I will recognize them by their light that runs before them, on their right and on their left."

The apparent meaning of this report is that the light is specific to the believers of this community, and likewise the giving of the books in the right hand. Some reports require that it belongs to every believer. Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Abu Umamah, who said: "Darkness will be sent forth on the Day of Resurrection, so no believer or disbeliever sees his palm until Allah, exalted is He, sends forth light for the believers according to the measure of their deeds." The report continues. Al-Hakim, who declared it authentic, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported it from him by another route, and Ibn al-Mubarak and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat* reported a lengthy report from him also containing what is apparent in generality. Likewise, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Ba'th* reported from Ibn Abbas, who said: "While people were in darkness, Allah, exalted is He, sent forth a light. When the believers saw the light they turned toward it, and the light was a guide for them from Allah, mighty and majestic is He, to Paradise." This report does not contradict their passing over the Sirat with their light, as is not hidden. Likewise the giving of the books in the right hand. In *Hidayat al-Murid li-Jawharat al-Tawhid*: the apparent sense of the verses and the hadiths is that it is not specific to this community, meaning the taking of the scrolls, although some scholars hesitated about it. End of quotation.

It may be said: what belongs to this community of the light is clearer than the light that belongs to others, or it is distinguished by another kind of distinction. As for the giving of the books in the right hand, perhaps it is because of its abundance among them compared to the rest of the nations, by which they are recognized. There are other discussions on this topic which will be mentioned, if Allah, exalted is He, wills, in their place. It was said: by the light is meant the Qur'an. Al-Dahhak said: the light is a metaphor for the guidance and the good pleasure in which they are. Sahl ibn Shu'ayb al-Sahmi and Abu Haywah read "*wa-bi-imanihim*" with a kasra on the hamzah. Abu Hayyan explained this as: the adverbial phrase "between their hands" is related to an omitted element, and the conjunction is upon it on that basis, i.e. "existing between their hands and existing by means of their faith." And that is, as you see, [weak]. Perhaps it is related to the implied saying in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Your good news today is gardens﴾, i.e. and because of their faith it is said to them that. The clause of the saying is either conjoined to what precedes it, or is a resumption, or is circumstantial, and on the circumstantial reading it is permissible to estimate the qualifier from it, i.e. "said to them." The sayer is the angels who receive them.

By "good news" is meant what one is given good news of, not the act of giving good news. The speech is with an omitted modifier, i.e. what you are given good news of is the entry into gardens, which is valid without it, i.e. what you are given good news of is gardens, which is also valid without it. As for what was said, that good news is not with regard to physical things, there is a point to be considered here. Estimating the modifier does not dispense with interpreting "good news", because giving good news is not the same as entering. The clause of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿flowing beneath them are rivers﴾ is in the position of a qualifier for "gardens." His saying, glorified is He: ﴿abiding therein﴾ is a circumstantial clause from "gardens." Abu Hayyan said: in the speech there is a shift (*iltifat*) from the pronoun of address in ﴿your good news﴾ to the pronoun of the absent in "abiding", and if it had been kept to address, the construction would have been "abiding, you therein." ﴿That is the supreme triumph﴾ may be from His own speech, exalted is He, so the reference is to what was mentioned of the light and the good news of the gardens. And it may be from the speech of the angels, peace be upon them, who receive them, so the reference is to what they are in of the light and other things, or to the gardens by interpreting what was mentioned, or because they are a triumph, as it was said. It was also read: "that triumph" without "huwa".

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 57, verse 13:

Page 176

﴿The Day when the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿the Day you will see﴾, and it is permitted that it be an object (ma'mul) of "udhkur" (remember).

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: It appears to me that the governing element (al-'amil) in it is that "great triumph" (al-fawz al-'azim), and the meaning of the triumph is greater upon it, as if it were said: The believers will triumph on the Day when the hypocrite men and hypocrite women are afflicted with such-and-such, because a person's ascendancy on the day of his enemy's humiliation is more marvelous and more splendid.

Abu Hayyan (in al-Bahr) criticized him, saying: The apparent sense of his explanation is that the Day (yawm) is governed by "al-fawz" (triumph), and this is not permitted, because it is a verbal noun (masdar) that has been described before its complements were taken, so it may not govern. Even if its descriptive adjective, "al-'azim" (great), were to govern, it would be permitted – i.e., the triumph that was great – i.e., its extent was great on the Day it ended. There is a disagreement about whether such a verbal noun may govern such an object. Then, the attachment of this adverbial phrase to something within that sentence is contrary to the apparent meaning. ﴿It will be said to those who believed: "Wait for us"﴾, i.e., wait for us, ﴿"that we may borrow from your light"﴾, i.e., that we may be given some of it. That is, that they may catch up with them and be illuminated by it.

It was said: that they may take from it something that will be with them; they imagined that this was possible, so they said it. The root of iqtibas (borrowing) is seeking a qabas, i.e., a brand or ember of fire. It is also permitted that the meaning be: "Look at us, that we may borrow etc.", because when they look at them, they face them with their faces, and the light is before them, so they are illuminated by it. Thus "anzurona" (look at us) is with ellipsis and transitivity, because looking in the sense of mere seeing is transitive with "ila" (to); if contemplation is intended, it is transitive with "fi". However, interpreting the verse in that way is contrary to the apparent meaning. And their saying "to the believers" is because they are in darkness and do not know how to walk in it. It is narrated that this will be at the Sirat (bridge).

There is evidence in the reports that they will have a light which is then extinguished, so they say this. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah will call people on the Day of Resurrection by their mothers, as a veil over them from His servants. As for at the Sirat, Allah says: He gives every believer a light and every hypocrite a light. When they are level upon the Sirat, Allah extinguishes the light of the hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the hypocrites say: 'Look at us, that we may borrow from your light.' And the believers say: 'Complete for us our light.' And at that point no one mentions anyone else."

In another marfu' hadith from him as well: "Indeed the light of the hypocrite is extinguished before he reaches the Sirat."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Abu Fakhitah: "Allah the Exalted gathers the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah, glorified is He, sends upon the people darkness, so they seek help from their Lord. Allah the Exalted gives every believer among them a light, and gives the hypocrites a light. They set out together, heading toward Paradise with their light. While they are thus, Allah extinguishes the light of the hypocrites, so they wander in the darkness, and the believers outpace them with their light before them. So they say: 'Look at us, that we may borrow from your light,' the report..." The reports concerning Allah giving the hypocrite a light and then extinguishing it are numerous, and there is nothing in the verse that contradicts it.

Zayd ibn 'Ali, Ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Talhah and Hamzah read "Anzirona" with a hamzah of cutting, a fatha, and a kasra on the zay, from al-nazirah, which is respite. It is said: "Anzir al-madyun," i.e., grant him respite. The phrase "Anzirona" is used in the sense of a pause and of a creditor granting respite to a debtor, in the place of a companion's slow, leisurely pace so that his companion may catch up with him, by way of metaphor, after a comparison of one state to another, as an exaggeration of helplessness and the display of need. It was also said: it is from anzara, i.e., to delay, and the meaning is: make us come last, and do not outpace us such that you leave us behind, and we do not catch up with you. Al-Mahdawi said: "Anzirona" and "Unzurona" have the same meaning, and both are from waiting (intizar). The Arabs say: "Anzartuhu bi-kadha" and "intazartuhu" have one meaning, and the meaning is: grant us respite.

﴿It will be said﴾ – the sayers, according to what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, are the believers, and according to what is narrated from Muqatil, they are the angels, peace be upon them.

﴿"Return behind you and seek light there."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: i.e., from where you came, from the darkness, or to the place where the light was divided, as is sound from Abu Umamah. Muqatil said: this is of the mockery directed at them, just as they mocked the believers in the world when they said "We believe" while they were not believers. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah mocks them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 15], i.e., when it is said to them: return behind you and seek light. Abu Umamah said: They return when it is said to them that, to the place where the light was divided, and they find nothing, so they turn back to them, and between them a wall has been struck, which is the deception of Allah, the Exalted, by which He deceived the hypocrites, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿They seek to deceive Allah, but He is their deceiver﴾ [al-Nisa': 142]. It was also said: the intended meaning is "Return to the world and seek light," i.e., by acquiring its cause, which is faith; or "Withdraw from us and seek light other than this, for there is no path for you to borrow from it." The purpose is also mockery and derision.

It was said: they meant by "light" what is behind them of the dense darkness, mocking them, but this is contrary to the apparent meaning. In any case, the apparent meaning is that "waraakum" (behind you) is an object of "irji'u" (return).

It was said: it has no place in the i'rab, because it has the meaning of "irji'u," so it is as if it were said: "Return, return," like their saying "waraaka awsa'u laka," i.e., return and you will find a wider place for you.

﴿Then a wall will be struck between them﴾, i.e., between the two groups. Zayd ibn 'Ali and 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr read "Fa-darab" in the active voice, i.e., He struck, He, that is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿with a wall﴾, i.e., with a barrier. Ibn Zayd said: it is al-A'raf. Others said: it is a barrier other than that, and the ba' is extra (za'idah). ﴿It has a gate, its inner part﴾, i.e., the gate, as narrated from Muqatil, or the wall, which is the side facing the place of the believers, namely Paradise, ﴿in it is mercy﴾, the reward and bliss which cannot be fully comprehended. ﴿And its outer part﴾, the side facing the place of the hypocrites, namely the Fire, ﴿before it is torment﴾. And this wall is said to be, in that state of existence and transformation of this world and the variation of its conditions, at the location of the eastern wall of the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Abu Sinan who said: I was with 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas at the Valley of Jahannam, meaning the well-known place near Bayt al-Maqdis, and he related from his father that he said, while reciting the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them﴾: "This is the place of the wall at the Valley of Jahannam." He and Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) and others narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As who said: The wall which Allah the Exalted mentioned in the Qur'an, ﴿So a wall will be struck between them﴾, is the eastern wall of Bayt al-Maqdis. ﴿Its inner part, in it is mercy﴾: the mosque. ﴿And its outer part, before it is torment﴾: meaning the Valley of Jahannam and what is adjacent to it.

He also narrated from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit that he was on the eastern wall of Bayt al-Maqdis and wept. It was said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "Here the Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed us that he saw Jahannam."

It is not hidden that this and similar matters are based on the difference of the two worlds and the variance of the two modes of existence, in a manner by which the intellects cannot reach comprehension of its modality or the knowledge of its details. If the report is authentic, we have no choice but to believe, since the matter does not fall outside the sphere of possibility. Abu Hayyan related, from one whom I have heard, and from Ka'b al-Ahbar, that it is the eastern wall of the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, and he found this unlikely, then said: "And perhaps it is not authentic from them."

﴿يُنادُونَهُمْ﴾ (They call out to them) is a resumptive clause (*isti'naf*, a new sentence that answers an implied question), as if it were said: "What will they do after the wall is set up and they witness the punishment?" The answer is: the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women call out to the believing men and the believing women: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾ in the world, meaning that they intend by this their agreement with them outwardly. ﴿They will say: Yes﴾, you were with us as you claim. ﴿But you led yourselves into temptation﴾, you tried yourselves with hypocrisy and destroyed yourselves, ﴿and you waited﴾ for the believers to suffer misfortunes, ﴿and you doubted﴾ and were uncertain about the matters of religion, ﴿and vain desires deceived you﴾, empty wishes, among which is the hope for the collapse of Islam.

[p. 178]

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿You led yourselves into temptation﴾ means through desires and pleasures. ﴿And you waited﴾ means for repentance. ﴿And you doubted﴾: Mahbub al-Laythi said: you doubted in God. ﴿And vain desires deceived you﴾ means the long-held hopes. Abu Sinan said: you said, "We will be forgiven." ﴿Until the command of God came﴾, that is, death. ﴿And the Deceiver deceived you about God﴾: this is Satan, who said to you: "God is Most Forgiving and Generous and will not punish you."

From Qatada: they were in a deception from Satan. By God, they remained in it until God cast them into the Fire.

Simak ibn Harb read *al-Ghurur* (the Deceiver) with a *damma*. Ibn Jinni said: it is like His saying ﴿and the Deceiver deceived you about God﴾, *al-ightirar* (the state of being deceived). Its underlying form, by omitting the modified noun (*hadhf al-mudaf*), is: "and the safety of being deceived about God deceived you," meaning: your being deceived by it was your safety (or: your safety from it was your deception).

Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 57, verse 15:

﴿So on that Day no ransom will be taken from you﴾, O hypocrites, ﴿nor from those who disbelieved﴾. ﴿Ransom﴾ (fidyah) means a compensation, which is what is given to preserve the self from calamity. The verb governing "the Day," the act negated by "lā," is what it is; and in this there is a proof against those who forbid that. Abu Ja'far, al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, al-A'raj, Ibn 'Amir and Harun, on the authority of Abu 'Amr, read "lā tu'khadhu" with the feminine (ta' fawqiyyah). ﴿Nor from those who disbelieved﴾, that is, outwardly and inwardly, so it is different from the addressees, the hypocrites. Then, the apparent meaning is that by "ransom" is meant what is of the kind of wealth and the like; but it is permitted that by it be meant what encompasses faith and repentance, and then the verse indicates that their faith and repentance will not be accepted on the Day of Resurrection. In this there is remoteness.

And in the hadith: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, says to the disbeliever: Tell Me, if you had the equivalent of the whole world, would you ransom yourself with all of that from the punishment of the Fire? He says: Yes, my Lord. Allah, blessed and exalted, says: I asked you for what is easier than that, while you were in the loins of your father Adam: that you should not associate anything with Me, but you refused except association."

﴿Your abode is the Fire﴾, the place of your residence. ﴿Huwa mawlakum﴾ (it is your protector), that is, your helper, from the pattern of "a painful beating is their greeting." The intent is the absolute negation of a helper, after the negation of taking a ransom and of their deliverance from punishment by it. Similar to this is the saying: "He was afflicted with such-and-such, so the panic sought help," and from it is the Most High's saying: ﴿They will be relieved with water like molten brass﴾ [al-Kahf: 29].

Al-Kalbi, al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and Abu 'Ubaydah said: that is, "more deserving of you," as in the verse of Labid describing a wild cow that fled from the sound of the hunter:

*So she became, with both her flanks, thinking that he was the mawla of fear, behind her and before her.*

That is, both her sides, behind and in front, she thought he was more deserving that fear should be in him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The real meaning of "mawlakum" according to this is "mahrakum" and "maqmanakum," that is, the place of which it is said: "He is more deserving of you," just as it is said: "It is a place of generosity," that is, a place for the speaker's saying: "Indeed he is generous." So "awlā" is a type of noun of place in which the meaning of "awlā" is considered, except that it is derived from it, just as "mi'nah" is not derived from the verb "inn" (the verifying particle). In the Tafsir al-Kabir: their saying that is an explanation of the resulting meaning and not an explanation of the word, for if "mawlā" and "awlā" had one meaning in the language, it would be valid to use each of them in the place of the other, and it would have to be valid to say "awlā fulān" as one says "hadha mawlā fulān." Since that is invalid, we know that what they said is a meaning and not an explanation. Then he clearly stated that he intended by this to refute al-Sharif al-Murtada's use of the hadith of Ghadir, "Whoever I am the mawla of, 'Ali is his mawla," as proof of the Imamate of the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah honour his face, since he said: "One of the meanings of mawla is awlā."

And to take it in the report to mean this is definite, for to intend other than it makes the report pointless, like the intent of "helper," "companion" and "cousin," or makes it a lie, like "the one who frees" and "the one who is freed." It is not hidden from the fair-minded that if by its being a meaning and not an explanation he meant what al-Zamakhshari pointed to of the verification, then it does not refute the argument, since it suffices for al-Murtada to say: "mawla" in the report means the place of which "awlā" is said, since otherwise it would entail pointlessness or lying for others. And if he meant that this is a necessary meaning of what is the explanation of it, such as that its explanation is "the one who stands over your interests" and the like, of which this is a necessary concomitant, then in his refuting the argument too there is hesitation. And if he meant something else, then we do not know what it is, and he has not clarified it. The truth is that even if "mawlā" is taken to mean "awlā" or the place of which "awlā" is said, the argument from the report for the Imamate that the Imamiyyah claim for the Commander of the Faithful, may Allah honour his face, is not complete, for reasons explained in its proper place. In the Twelver work *al-Tuhfah* there is what is sufficient for the seeker of truth.

Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, your destination.
